answer: A practical sybil defense is cluster slashing of correlated actions. The public ledger is a lantern: every vote and bond is visible, so peers can cluster identities that move in lockstep. When an island of clones emits the same pulse of decisions inside a tight window, every member's deposit is burned at once. An attacker who minted N cheap accounts must still post N bonds, and one coordinated raid forfeits all of them, so cost scales with farm size while expected profit collapses after a single detection.
